correctness.rationale: Source equations (14)--(23) give mu_k=mu because g is identically zero, soft threshold x^+=0, eta=x/mu. In one scalar dimension beta*d_old=gamma*y_old exactly when denominator is nonzero, so d=-eta. With |x|<=mu*lambda/max(1,T), the first trial t=1 satisfies -lambda|x|/mu <= -T*x^2/mu^2; and the stronger usual decrease inequality at alpha=1 holds since delta<1 and |x|<=mu*lambda. Crucial source nuance: printed Eq. (23) is f_new <= f_old - delta*alpha*eta^T*d; for d=-eta its right side is f_old+delta*alpha*eta^2, so the directly proved stronger decrease also guarantees the printed inequality despite the RESULT.md phrase treating the two as equivalent. On the recurrence y=d/mu and z=y+nu*d, denominator d*z=d^2*(1/mu+nu)>0. The contraction is strictly between 0 and 1; practical tolerance eventually terminates, unlike exact-stationarity stopping.
residual_risks: The prose in RESULT.md paraphrases the source Eq. (23) sign as a stronger conventional decrease condition; the theorem remains true because that stronger condition holds. Correct the explanatory equation in a future fully guarded scientific-file update.
The scalar g=0 case and exact-stationarity stopping do not determine high-dimensional identification or practical stop counts.

value.rationale: The precise failure of finite activity identification despite an exact soft-threshold hit is a motivated algorithmic boundary: line-search descent and convergence need not preserve the active-set identification of the computed prox point. The counterexample is canonical for sparse optimization and shows an arbitrarily slow tail as mu grows, rather than a gratuitous numerical substitution.
residual_risks: The model is one-dimensional and not a demonstrated defect in practical positive-tolerance LASSO runs; the source makes no finite-identification guarantee.

final_claim: For Algorithm 3.1 (called Algorithm 2 in the rendered preprint) of Hamana--Narushima with g=0,h=lambda|x|,mu_{-1}=mu>1 and nonzero |x0|<=mu*lambda/max(1,T), the exact-step NCG branch has x_k^+=0 but x_k=(1-1/mu)^k x0 !=0 for every finite k; both line-search stages accept 1 and the fallback proximal update would stop in one update.
